title: feat(scval): fully decode and render maps and vectors
problem: Maps and vectors are decoded as raw serde JSON, which is hard to read and unstable.
why: Collections are common in contract data and must be rendered clearly.
context: Decoding uses `stellar-xdr`; rendering is a curated layer.
scope: Render vectors and maps recursively with bounded depth
Handle nested and empty collections
guidance: Bound recursion; report depth limits explicitly.
acceptance: Collections render deterministically with a documented depth cap
tests: Unit tests for empty, nested, and deep collections
security: Bound recursion to prevent stack exhaustion.
docs: Document rendering in the SCVal guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(scval): decode and render addresses and contract IDs
problem: Address values render as raw bytes rather than strkeys.
why: Developers expect account/contract addresses, not byte arrays.
scope: Render account and contract addresses as strkeys
Label unknown address kinds explicitly
guidance: Never guess an address kind; report what the XDR says.
acceptance: Addresses render as strkeys with correct kinds
tests: Round-trip tests for account and contract addresses
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(xdr): inspect TransactionResult and TransactionMeta
problem: Result and metadata XDR cannot be inspected, so failures cannot be diagnosed.
why: Result and meta XDR are required for meaningful transaction analysis.
scope: Decode TransactionResult and TransactionMeta from base64
Expose a CLI command and JSON output
acceptance: Result and meta decode with structured errors
tests: Fixture-based tests including an unknown version
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(xdr): inspect diagnostic events
problem: Diagnostic events embedded in transaction meta cannot be inspected.
why: Diagnostic events explain contract failures and are high-value for debugging.
context: Contract event decoding exists; diagnostic events do not.
scope: Decode diagnostic events from meta
Render topics and data with the curated renderer
out_of_scope: Correlating diagnostics to specific host calls.
guidance: Distinguish diagnostic from contract events clearly.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(xdr): pretty-print ledger entries
problem: Ledger entries fetched from RPC cannot be printed readably.
why: Readable ledger entries are needed for storage inspection.
scope: Decode and render common ledger entry types
Fall back to raw output for unsupported types
guidance: State exactly which entry types are rendered.
acceptance: Documented entry types render; others fall back
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(scval): add type-safe conversions between SCVal and Rust primitives
problem: Extracting a Rust value from an SCVal requires manual matching.
why: Typed accessors make analysis code safer and shorter.
context: SCVal has many variants; conversions must be explicit.
scope: Provide typed accessors for common primitives with precise errors
Never coerce lossily
acceptance: Accessors cover documented primitive variants with precise errors
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(xdr): distinguish envelope v0 and v1 variants
problem: Envelope inspection treats all variants uniformly, obscuring v0/v1 differences.
why: Soroban transactions are v1 and require different handling than classic v0.
context: TransactionEnvelope is an enum with multiple variants.
scope: Expose the envelope variant explicitly in output
Reject Soroban-only operations in v0 where invalid
guidance: Report the variant as a confirmed fact.
acceptance: Variant is reported; invalid combinations are handled
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(xdr): validate bytes, symbol, and string lengths
problem: Length limits for symbols and strings are not enforced when reporting values.
why: Invalid lengths indicate malformed or hostile input and should be flagged, not silently rendered.
context: Soroban enforces length limits at runtime; the toolkit should surface violations.
scope: Validate symbol/string/bytes lengths against documented limits
Report violations as diagnostics
guidance: Use the documented limits and cite them.
tests: Boundary tests at and beyond limits
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(transactions): extract source account and sequence number
problem: There is no structured extraction of the source account or sequence number.
why: These are the first facts a developer needs when inspecting a transaction.
context: Envelope decoding exists but is not summarized structurally.
scope: Extract source account (strkey) and sequence number
Report them in the envelope summary and JSON
guidance: Report only fields present in the envelope.
acceptance: Source and sequence are extracted for all envelope variants
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(transactions): inspect operations with type-specific detail
problem: Operations are not individually inspected or summarized.
why: Operations are the substance of a transaction; developers need per-operation detail.
context: Envelopes contain a list of operations of many types.
scope: Summarize each operation with common fields
Provide type-specific detail for the most common operation types
guidance: Document exactly which operation types are detailed.
acceptance: Common operation types render with type-specific fields
tests: Fixture-based tests per covered operation type
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(transactions): analyze fees (base, resource, and total)
problem: Fee fields are not summarized, and Soroban resource fees are separate from base fees.
why: Fee visibility is important for cost debugging.
context: Soroban transactions include a resource fee in the Soroban data.
scope: Report base fee, resource fee, and computed total per operation/transaction
Document how the total is derived
guidance: Never present a derived value as confirmed; label it as a computed total.
acceptance: Fees are reported with a documented derivation
tests: Tests for classic and Soroban transactions
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(transactions): inspect signatures and signer hints
problem: Signatures are not inspected, and signer identification is unclear.
why: Understanding who signed (or which hints are present) is part of reviewing a transaction.
context: Decorated signatures carry 4-byte hints; verification requires key material not in the envelope.
scope: Report the number of signatures and their hints
State explicitly that hints do not identify signers and that verification is not performed
guidance: Do not overclaim: hints are not identities.
acceptance: Signature count and hints are reported with honest limitations
tests: Tests including an unsigned and a multi-signed envelope
security: Avoid implying verification; documents the boundary.
docs: Document limitations in the transactions guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(transactions): handle memo and time/ledger bounds
problem: Memos and validity bounds are not summarized.
why: Memos and bounds affect whether and how a transaction is valid.
context: Envelopes carry a memo and optional time/ledger bounds.
scope: Render all memo types
Render time and ledger bounds when present
guidance: Render memo text safely; bound its length.
acceptance: Memo and bounds render for all variants
tests: Tests per memo type and with/without bounds
security: Escape or bound memo text in terminal output.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(transactions): inspect Soroban transaction data and footprint
problem: Soroban-specific transaction data (resource fees and footprint) is not inspected.
why: The footprint determines which ledger entries a transaction touches; it is central to Soroban analysis.
scope: Decode and summarize footprint (read-only and read-write entries)
Report resource fee and resource limits if present
guidance: Render ledger keys readably where supported; otherwise show raw.
acceptance: Footprint and resource data are summarized
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(transactions): interpret transaction results and failure codes
problem: Result codes are not mapped to human explanations.
why: Failure diagnosis is one of the most common developer needs.
context: Result XDR carries per-operation and transaction result codes.
scope: Map known result codes to short explanations
Report unknown codes verbatim
out_of_scope: Guaranteeing the root cause of a failure.
guidance: Keep the mapping data-driven and documented; never invent meanings.
acceptance: Known codes are explained; unknown codes pass through
tests: Tests for representative success and failure codes
docs: Document the code table in the transactions guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.
